prompt.root: You are Prime Agent. This is one independent top-level ARC-AGI-3 OFFLINE session. First read and follow /workspace/AGENTS.md exactly; it is the pinned generic V3 PRO-LONG game guidance. The document's legacy reference to an RLM child does not authorize an RLM call here: you are already the sole top-level session. Use only /workspace/fixed_broker_client.py, which exposes only observe(), status(), and act(actions) for this fixed game. It has no game ID, capability, prepare, lifecycle, scorecard, inventory, or other-game API. Do not call RLM, create agents, use agent_message, access network/credentials/source/other sessions, or use mocks, ARC online APIs, Competition mode, or scorecards. Continue through the fixed broker until WIN or ACTION_CAP.
prompt.repository_instructions:
# ARC-AGI-3 Local Game Behavioral Guidance

This guidance applies to every game-playing RLM child. You are a coding agent playing one grid-based puzzle game through the capability-scoped local broker. Your primary objective is to solve all levels. Your secondary objective is to minimize total cumulative actions.

Treat only your broker observations and your own retained session as game information. Never inspect game or engine source, another game, another session, a prior run, network resources, or unprovided files. Your IPython kernel and conversation are private persistent scratch state: retain concise notes, helper functions, hypotheses, fixed-cell histories, and component analyses there. Do not read from or write game notes to the provider-shared `/workspace`.

The broker returns action count, state, completed-level count, available actions, recent executed actions, and frames. A completed-level increase means a level was cleared. A response may contain animation frames; frame 1/N through frame N/N are temporal frames, and the final frame is the settled committed state. Analyze frames programmatically rather than relying on visual transcription. Useful methods include colors, connected components, positions, sizes, shapes, fixed-cell histories, and before/after or distant-turn diffs.

Cell values use the canonical ARC color map: 0 White, 1 Off-White, 2 Light Gray, 3 Gray, 4 Off-Black, 5 Black, 6 Magenta, 7 Light Magenta, 8 Red, 9 Blue, 10 Light Blue, 11 Yellow, 12 Orange, 13 Maroon, 14 Green, 15 Purple.

Action semantics are fixed: ACTION1 is Up, ACTION2 is Down, ACTION3 is Left, ACTION4 is Right, ACTION5 is Spacebar/interact, ACTION6 is a click at column x and row y, ACTION7 is Undo, and RESET resets the current level while still consuming one action. For ACTION1–ACTION5, ACTION7, and RESET, use an empty data object. ACTION6 must use integer coordinates exactly as `{"name":"ACTION6","data":{"x":30,"y":40}}`, with x and y in 0–63; never send ACTION6 with missing or empty coordinate data. Numeric available-action values correspond to ACTION1–ACTION7.

Maintain a world model: identify likely player, walls, goals, hazards, UI, interaction rules, timers, and how each test changed the settled state. Games may produce GAME_OVER from a step budget or timer. The trusted broker stops the old batch, performs exactly one counted RESET when budget remains, and returns the fresh observation. It also stops and flushes the old batch immediately when the completed-level count increases. Reassess every fresh level or reset before acting again; never carry queued actions blindly across either boundary.

Before every action call, give a concise strategic briefing followed by `[PLAN]` and 2–3 sentences stating the current hypothesis, expected change, shortest useful test, and remaining-budget implications. Prefer batches of 1–2 actions for new hypotheses. Use a longer batch, at most 20, only for a sequence already supported by observations. After every broker response, inspect the returned batch trace and settled observation, compare expected with observed changes, update retained notes, and formulate a new plan. Never use Python or shell loops to submit actions. Never repeat an unchanged or losing sequence without a new evidence-based reason.

Continue autonomously until the broker reports WIN or ACTION_CAP. Do not stop merely because a hypothesis failed, no progress occurred, or a tool call was rejected. Use only your assigned broker capability. Do not call RLM or create agents. Do not use mocks, ARC online APIs, Competition mode, or scorecards.

bootstrap: one genuine non-RESET action if still ACTIVE

autonomous_continuation_rule.generic_runtime: Same AgentSession/currentContext follow-up after tool loop quiesces if gates/limits permit
autonomous_continuation_rule.default_prompt: No human input is available in autonomous mode. Continue working until the host evaluator, verifier, or configured autonomous limits stop the run. If you were asking the user a question, make a reasonable assumption and verify it. If you believe you are blocked, prove it with host-observable evidence, preserve that evidence, and keep looking for safe progress while budget remains. Do not end the session yourself; the verifier/evaluator decides completion when configured gates pass.

token_accounting_rule.generic_autonomous: input + output + cacheWrite; excludes cacheRead; assistant message_end, except error

persistence_semantics.within_launch: Broker Handle, AgentSession/currentContext and kernel retained

questions.question: Which environment/game set?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: Published results contain the same 25 fully versioned public game IDs in each of three Opus runs. Broker selects the first local corpus environment whose ID starts with the requested prefix. No corpus file hashes or selection manifest are provided; Figure 5 correspondence is unproven.

questions.question: Exactly how many games?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: 25 entries in each published run; run.sh launches ONE requested game and has no all-25 scheduler or task-count assertion.

questions.question: Seed/start-state behavior?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: Broker creates Arcade(OFFLINE), calls make(resolved, seed=0, save_recording=True, include_frame_data=True), then env.reset(). Handle.actions starts at zero, so this explicit initial reset is not charged to its 500-action counter. No further trajectory initialization is in dispatch.

questions.question: Root prompt?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: Exact game-prompt.txt and AGENTS.md are embedded in this spec. They forbid RLM/agent creation, prescribe programmatic frame analysis and pre-action plans, and instruct continuation until WIN or ACTION_CAP. Prompt expects /workspace/fixed_broker_client.py; launcher only copies broker_client.py to a different workspace path. RPC startup does not submit its positional prompt.

questions.question: Environment tools/actions?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: Client exposes observe(), status(), act(actions). Bootstrap requires observe, then a single non-RESET act, then a second single non-RESET act if still ACTIVE. Broker accepts RESET and ACTION1..7, batches 1..20, ACTION6 x/y integers 0..63. Observations include raw frames, state, levels_completed, available_actions, action count/remaining, terminal, and game_id (contrary to prompt description). Published broker does not return the batch trace promised by guidance.

questions.question: What constitutes one agent turn?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: runLoop emits turn_start, generates one assistant response, executes its tool-call batch, then emits turn_end. addAutonomousUsage increments turnsUsed at non-error assistant message_end. This is not an entire RPC prompt or an entire game.

questions.question: What causes another autonomous turn?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: Tool results/steering continue the inner loop. When that loop would finish and no queued follow-ups exist, _getContinuationMessages calls nextAutonomousContinuation. With no gates and remaining limits it appends the generic autonomous user continuation. The provided run.sh sets --autonomous but no gate/limit overrides.

questions.question: Exact end-condition after a turn?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: _shouldStopAfterTurn handles goal state, serialized refinement, and compaction. Autonomous quality gates run at continuation selection, not unconditionally after every tool-bearing turn. Client terminal-gate succeeds for WIN or ACTION_CAP, but run.sh never configures it. An ARC host terminal test for the reported evaluation is absent.

questions.question: What stops a game?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: Broker revokes further mutations at WIN or ACTION_CAP. GAME_OVER triggers a counted reset if budget remains and flushes the batch. This does not itself terminate the agent process. Root prompt says stop at WIN/ACTION_CAP, but actual reported host stop wiring is missing.

questions.question: Action limits?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: Executable broker cap is 500 cumulative actions, max 20 per call; each reset consumes one except initialization. A level-count change, GAME_OVER reset, WIN, or cap flushes the batch. Results contradict the 500 cap: 7/9/7 games across runs exceed it; maximum is 5000.

questions.question: Token limits?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: Launcher supplies none. Runtime v0.3.3 fallback autonomous limits: 3 continuations, 12 assistant turns, 80000 non-cache-read tokens, 1800000 ms. These bound autonomous continuation admission, not an actively generating tool loop. External/user settings and exact reported-run limits are missing.

questions.question: Output tokens only or total?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: Generic autonomous counter uses input + output + cacheWrite, excludes cacheRead. It is not an output-only scaling cap. getSessionStats totals input + output + cacheRead + cacheWrite. Figure 5 expenditure selection is not implemented in the published ARC code.

questions.question: Root + descendants?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: ARC prompt explicitly forbids descendants. General Prime runtime can attribute child usage into a parent assistant entry, but that does not establish Figure 5 aggregation. The public ARC result export has no root/child breakdown or exporter.

questions.question: Compaction/refinement/subagent calls counted?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: Generic autonomous usage callback counts assistant message_end, not all provider calls. generateSummary and refinement helpers call completeSimple and return text/parsed edits, discarding response usage at those boundaries. A separate Figure 5 usage collector could differ, but none is published. Do not equate this counter with paper accounting.

questions.question: Cumulative output thresholds per game?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: No output-threshold array, threshold monitor, or per-snapshot output-token data exists in the ARC repository. results.json contains only total output tokens per full run.

questions.question: Figure 5 checkpoints from one trajectory?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: No code establishes this. Broker and generic autonomous continuations retain state within one launch, but no curve collector links token thresholds to that state.

questions.question: Figure 5 independent fresh runs?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: No code establishes this either. Three distinct Opus result objects and fresh_run_per_game=true are not evidence that each curve point is a fresh run.

questions.question: When/how is a checkpoint snapshotted?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: No snapshot collector or RHAE-versus-token plotting implementation. The HTML only displays final scalar values from JSON.

questions.question: Can a response end while the game continues?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: Yes in generic autonomous runtime: an ordinary final assistant response can be followed by another user continuation if gates/limits permit. Broker environment remains alive. End-to-end ARC wiring is not established because the launcher lacks its RPC driver.

questions.question: Next continuation prompt?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: The generic DEFAULT_AUTONOMOUS_CONTINUATION_PROMPT is embedded below. Configured failed gates instead use buildAutonomousGateFailureContinuation with command, attempt, bounded output, timestamp. ARC launcher provides no custom continuation prompt or gate.

questions.question: Same model session survives?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: Generic runLoop appends continuation messages to currentContext and invokes the same AgentSession. It does not create a new session at an autonomous continuation. No evidence identifies the Figure 5 checkpoint/session boundaries.

questions.question: Same REPL survives?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: AgentSession retains its IPython kernel provisioner across ordinary turns; continuation hooks do not rebuild it. Reload has separate replacement logic. ARC prompt explicitly directs retention in private IPython state. No checkpoint collector is available to prove that behavior across Figure 5 points.

questions.question: Same ARC environment survives?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: Broker stores one Handle.env across all observe/status/act requests. It only resets in response to RESET or GAME_OVER recovery, within that same wrapper. Checkpoint lifecycle is unspecified.

questions.question: Compaction during same trajectory?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: General runtime supports in-session threshold compaction, preserves queued autonomous continuations, and resumes the same AgentSession. Published ARC launcher does not pin compaction/refinement settings and has no recorded trace of these events.

questions.question: Completion before a later checkpoint?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: Broker returns unchanged terminal observation on later act calls. There is no score carry-forward, early-completion cost treatment, or checkpoint aggregation code.

questions.question: Exact Best@1 semantics?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: No executable selection/aggregation definition. results.json contains three full Opus runs and identifies run-1 as median; the viewer selects that record. Do not infer per-game best, best run, single attempt, or interpolation semantics from the name Best@1.

questions.question: RHAE aggregation?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: No RHAE aggregation code is present. Viewer prints the stored rhae_percent scalar. Broker uses the official SDK internally, but never exports/closes/snapshots a scorecard for constructing the published scalar or curve.

questions.question: Partial levels/progress?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: Broker returns official observation.levels_completed and stops a batch whenever the count changes. Viewer displays levels_completed/total_levels. How partial levels enter Figure 5 RHAE, incomplete-game denominators, or missing-game handling is absent.

questions.question: Infrastructure failures/retries?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: Broker catches exceptions and returns ok=false; client raises; launcher contains no retry loop. Guard source has fatal-ambiguity termination and read-only status timeout handling, but run.sh never starts that guard. Generic runtime retries transient provider errors and recovers context overflow in the same session; exact evaluation retry/usage-disposition settings are unpinned.

questions.question: Cost/output-token curve construction?
questions.discovered_code_behavior: Missing collector, raw per-response/per-action trajectories, per-checkpoint data, model pricing manifest, interpolation/averaging rules, and plotting script. Only final Opus aggregate cost/output totals exist. No Sol/Terra/GLM Figure 5 result series are supplied.

comparison.prime_semantic: 25 versioned IDs in published result data
comparison.our_semantic: Same 25 IDs in installed local corpus
comparison.justification: Exact ID-set equality checked locally; byte-for-byte match to paper corpus remains unspecified.
Installed dependency versions match the published pyproject. Prime corpus content hashes are absent.

comparison.prime_semantic: One OFFLINE Arcade/Handle per broker, seed 0, make then explicit reset
comparison.our_semantic: Independent official subprocess/Arcade per attempt, make(seed); no second reset
comparison.justification: Worker isolation matches; initialization call sequence differs. Two normalized observation hashes match despite that difference; retry lifecycle is also different.

comparison.prime_semantic: Pinned game-prompt.txt + AGENTS.md, no delegation, pre-action PLAN
comparison.our_semantic: Generic benchmark_action task plus Buffalo tool instructions; delegation allowed
comparison.justification: Exact prompt text, guidance, and delegation constraints differ. Missing launcher prevents confirmation of the paper-effective prompt.

comparison.prime_semantic: Fixed Python observe/status/act, bootstrap, raw frames, batches <=20, GAME_OVER auto-reset
comparison.our_semantic: Dynamic benchmark_action(single action,data); raw frame plus RLE transport; explicit agent RESET
comparison.justification: Operation shape, bootstrap, batching, observations, and reset/level boundary handling differ.

comparison.prime_semantic: Generic same-session continuation until configured gates/limits; actual ARC driver missing
comparison.our_semantic: Codex stops at turn/completed; Buffalo stops at Runtime session completion for ARC
comparison.justification: Our evaluator does not re-prompt an unsolved game after ordinary completion. The exact paper host gate and limits are unspecified.

comparison.our_semantic: Only final scorecard; obsolete independent sweep controller disabled
comparison.justification: No evidence for continuing-vs-independent points, thresholds, crossing boundaries, or carry-forward. No parity claim is possible.

comparison.prime_semantic: Figure 5 UNSPECIFIED; generic autonomy input+output+cacheWrite, excludes cacheRead
comparison.our_semantic: All provider requests root+descendant+compaction+refinement, input/output recorded separately
comparison.justification: Generic counter is not paper expenditure evidence; silently adopting either would invent Figure 5 semantics.

comparison.prime_semantic: Broker terminal WIN/ACTION_CAP; GAME_OVER resets; host gate not wired
comparison.our_semantic: No host ARC-terminal stop; runner stops on agent completion or resource limits
comparison.justification: Broker end states and agent stop conditions differ; adding a guessed terminal driver cannot demonstrate exact parity.

comparison.prime_semantic: 500 in broker, contradicted by published results
comparison.justification: Budget values and counted entities differ. Prime paper-effective action budget requires its generating configuration.

comparison.our_semantic: Official EnvironmentScorecard.from_scorecard over disjoint final cards
comparison.justification: Our official scorer is concrete, but Prime exports only scalar results; its curve aggregation/Best@1 cannot be confirmed.

comparison.prime_semantic: No launcher retry loop; guard fatal ambiguity logic not launched; runtime provider retries configurable
comparison.our_semantic: Up to 3 fresh infrastructure-invalid attempts; failed usage retained separately
comparison.justification: Fresh-game retry behavior and accounting cannot be equated to the missing reported-run policy.

comparison.prime_semantic: Generic session/context/kernel persist; broker Handle persists; no checkpoint lifecycle code
comparison.our_semantic: Same native thread/Runtime/Python/environment within attempt; fresh retry creates new state
comparison.justification: Within-attempt persistence exists in both. Persistence across curve points is unspecified and not implemented in our scheduler.

blockers.reason: No Figure 5 runner, snapshot collector, plotting script, checkpoint sequence, or four-model raw trajectory data in either discovered repository.
Published executable cap is 500; 23 of 75 published game records exceed it, up to 5000 actions. The generating run configuration is absent.
run.sh selects RPC mode without an RPC prompt driver, omits terminal-gate configuration, references the wrong client filename/path, and never starts the published protocol guard.
No code links root/auxiliary usage, official scorecard snapshots, per-game aggregation, partial progress, retries, Best@1, or prices to Figure 5.
Public result metadata names Prime v0.3.3, but no immutable generating-run manifest proves a runtime SHA, environment byte hashes, effective settings, or Figure 5 provenance.

initialization_audit.kind: official-environment initialization audit; no agent evaluation

execution.why_no_protocol_patch: Changing a runnable evaluator to incomplete/conflicting defaults would not reproduce Figure 5. Preserve existing implementation until the generating protocol is supplied.
